incident_context.architecture: Console stores linked external provider credentials and proxies requests through its gateway.
incident_context.caveat: The official X statement could not be fetched directly; its incident scope is reported by reposts. No root cause or supply-chain entry point was independently established. A server-side credential-store or gateway breach is a hypothesis consistent with the Console architecture, not a proven cause.

limitations: Accompanying cached JavaScriptCore/Bun bytecode was not independently decompiled or proven semantically equivalent to the extracted source.

Native upstream comparison rules out per-app changes within the compared bytes; it does not establish that upstream packages themselves are free of vulnerabilities or malicious behavior. No independent reproducible source builds were performed.

Disassembly focused on entrypoints, constructors, FFI exports and credential/network/process-related paths. Every instruction of Electron, Bun and native dependencies was not manually reviewed; indirect dispatch and CFG recovery limit static coverage.

No execution of the application, live authenticated config capture, incident-time traffic, backend source/logs or earlier compromised artifact was available. No historical-compromise or current-service safety verdict follows.
Static source inventory and literal endpoint searches cannot exclude runtime-generated destinations, configuration abuse, incidental telemetry leakage or code loaded after installation.
